items.title: 52060_Eddie Barefield oral history interview
items.q: We had become good friends, and he called me to come up and work with him at Freedom Land on tenor

ctx.x: Well, you know, what about the playing with Paul Laval, the Freedom --

Well, this comes next, 1963. I got a call that Paul Laval wanted a tenor player. Paul called me because I had worked with him in radio. We had become good friends, and he called me to come up and work with him at Freedom Land on tenor, so I bought a tenor. I didn't have one at the time.

And I bought the tenor, which I'm still playing, and went to Freedom Land. Now, during the time at Freedom Land Paul was telling me that the World Fair was coming in, and the next year after I was there, and he wanted a drummer. So the drummer that I took to South America with me, Sol Hall, I put him in touch with Sol. And Sol went out to the World Fair.

items.title: 52060_Eddie Barefield oral history interview
items.q: they all were playing with Paul Lavalle so I was playing with them.

ctx.x: Yeah, well, his brother Kermit Lavinsky. He studied with me and he was a fine tenor player. But he studied composition with me and he finally ended up in Hollywood writing for movies and pictures and everything. But he committed suicide a few years ago.

Then I had a lot of pupils. I was doing very good teaching and then I was working on the staff, too. Then finally Hank D'Amico and Vernon Brown and Billy Butterfield and a bunch of them came over on the staff and they all were playing with Paul Lavalle so I was playing with them. Then finally they gave Hank a band and I was the arranger. And I wrote a lot of things for that station while I was up there.

And then finally -- Hallwood said they hired me at that time because of the war, you know, and they wanted to make it look good that they had -- I was the only Negro in there, you know. They wanted to make it look good. So when the war was over, 1946 it was when I got my notice with 25 other men -- got their notice. And everybody was eventually hired back but me. And "Down Beat" had it in the paper, they said, well, with Barefield's seniority he should fight this. And I got a lot of calls to take up -- go back…
